title: Equivariant refinement of a fibre-separating product after principal localization
statement: Let $B\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that every element of $S$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $B$. Let a finite group $G$ act on $S$ by $B$-algebra automorphisms, and let $\mathfrak p\subset B$ be prime. Suppose there is a finite product decomposition $S\simeq\prod_{i=1}^n D_i$ of $B$-algebras, $n\geq1$, such that every $D_i$ has exactly one prime over $\mathfrak p$. No compatibility of this decomposition with $G$ is assumed. Then there exists $b\in B\setminus\mathfrak p$ and a finite family $(e_j)_{j\in J}$ in $S_b$ with $e_j^2=e_j$, $e_je_k=0$ for $j\ne k$, and $\sum_j e_j=1$, such that $s\mapsto(e_js)_j$ is a $B_b$-algebra isomorphism $S_b\simeq\prod_{j\in J}e_jS_b$, whose inverse is summation. The sets $D(e_j)=\{Q\in\operatorname{Spec}S_b:e_j\notin Q\}$ refine the original factor partition after localization, each contain exactly one prime over $\mathfrak pB_b$, and are permuted by $G$. Equivalently $G$ permutes the idempotents and factors. Contraction identifies the fibre primes before and after localization, preserving their residue fields and their $G$-action. In particular $|J|=n$, a chosen fibre prime remains in a chosen relabelled first factor, and purely inseparable residue extensions remain purely inseparable. Here spectra are as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $B_b=B[1/b]$, $S_b=S[1/\varphi(b)]$ for the given map $\varphi:B\to S$, and the residue field of a prime $Q$ is $\operatorname{Frac}(S/Q)$. No Noetherian or module-finiteness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0BST, lemma-inertia-invariants-etale, third reduction paragraph: equivariant refinement of clopen pieces and principal localization removing the empty-fibre pieces.

proof.text: Let $c_i\in S$ be the inverse images of the coordinate units of $\prod_iD_i$. Thus $c_i^2=c_i$, $c_ic_k=0$ for $i\ne k$, and $\sum_i c_i=1$. At any prime $Q$ exactly one $c_i$ is outside $Q$: at least one is outside because their sum is $1$, and at most one because their pairwise products vanish. If this index is $i$, every other factor lies in $Q$, and projection identifies $Q$ with a unique prime of $D_i$, preserving contraction to $B$. Consequently the fibre is exactly $\{Q_1,\ldots,Q_n\}$, with $Q_i$ the unique fibre prime in $D(c_i)$. These are statements about the prime-ideal spectrum of [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Tag 0BST, lemma-inertia-invariants-etale, third reduction paragraph (finite equivariant refinement and principal localization).

proof.text: For each function $\alpha:G\to\{1,\ldots,n\}$ put $f_\alpha=\prod_{g\in G}g(c_{\alpha(g)})$. The finite family is idempotent and pairwise orthogonal: if $\alpha(g)\ne\beta(g)$, the corresponding two factors have product $g(c_{\alpha(g)}c_{\beta(g)})=0$. Distributivity gives $\sum_\alpha f_\alpha=\prod_g\sum_i g(c_i)=1$. For $h\in G$ define $(h\alpha)(g)=\alpha(h^{-1}g)$; reindexing the product gives $h(f_\alpha)=f_{h\alpha}$. The factor at $g=1$ also gives $c_{\alpha(1)}f_\alpha=f_\alpha$, so $D(f_\alpha)\subset D(c_{\alpha(1)})$.

source.place: Tag 0BST, lemma-inertia-invariants-etale, third reduction paragraph (finite equivariant refinement and principal localization).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent], every $D(f_\alpha)$ is clopen. Orthogonality and the sum-one equation show that these subsets form a disjoint cover, allowing empty members. Every $Q_i$ belongs to exactly one of them, by the same prime-ideal argument as in step 1; each member contains at most one $Q_i$, because it lies in one $D(c_i)$. Let $J$ be the functions whose member meets the fibre. Then $J$ has exactly $n$ elements. The action on primes is $hQ=\{h(s):s\in Q\}$; since $h$ fixes $B$, contraction to $B$ is unchanged. Together with $h(f_\alpha)=f_{h\alpha}$, this proves that both $J$ and its complement are invariant under $G$.

proof.text:
The finite union $Z= igcup_{\alpha
otin J}D(f_\alpha)$ is closed and does not meet the fibre. The hypothesis about monic polynomials is exactly integrality, so [lem-weil-pbc-integral-spec-closed-map] makes its image $C$ in $\operatorname{Spec}B$ closed, with $\mathfrak p
otin C$. Apply the basis clause of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open] to choose $b
otin\mathfrak p$ such that $D(b)\subset\operatorname{Spec}B\setminus C$. The localization clause of that node identifies $\operatorname{Spec}S_b$ with $D(\varphi(b))\subset\operatorname{Spec}S$. This open is disjoint from $Z$: any point in their intersection would contract both into $D(b)$ and into $C$.

source.place: Tag 0BST, lemma-inertia-invariants-etale, third reduction paragraph (finite equivariant refinement and principal localization).

proof.text: Write $\bar f_\alpha$ for the image of $f_\alpha$ in $S_b$. For $\alpha\notin J$ the set $D(\bar f_\alpha)$ is empty by step 4. The uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent], applied to this idempotent and $0$, gives $\bar f_\alpha=0$. For $j\in J$ put $e_j=\bar f_j$. They remain orthogonal idempotents, and deleting the zero terms in the sum gives $\sum_{j\in J}e_j=1$. Contraction under localization identifies the fibre primes by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso], applied to $B\to B_b$ and $S\to S_b$: all the $Q_i$ survive because $\varphi(b)\notin Q_i$, and the square of localization maps commutes. Thus the contraction of $Q_iS_b$ to $B_b$ contracts to $\mathfrak p$ in $B$, so equals $\mathfrak pB_b$ by uniqueness in that prime correspondence. Conversely, a prime over $\mathfrak pB_b$ contracts in $S$ to one over $\mathfrak p$, hence to one of the $Q_i$. Thus each $D(e_j)$ still contains its unique fibre prime. It lies inside the localized original factor open since $c_{j(1)}f_j=f_j$.

source.place: Tag 0BST, lemma-inertia-invariants-etale, third reduction paragraph (finite equivariant refinement and principal localization).

proof.text: Give $e_jS_b=\{e_js:s\in S_b\}$ its induced addition and multiplication and unit $e_j$, with $B_b$-structure $a\mapsto e_j\varphi_b(a)$. The map $\Phi(s)=(e_js)_j$ preserves addition, multiplication, units and these scalar maps. For $x_j\in e_jS_b$, one has $e_jx_j=x_j$ and $e_kx_j=0$ for $k\ne j$. Hence $e_k\sum_jx_j=x_k$, whereas $\sum_je_js=s$. Thus summation is inverse to $\Phi$ and $\Phi$ is the required $B_b$-algebra isomorphism. Under this isomorphism the prime belonging to factor $j$ is precisely one with $e_j\notin Q$, by the coordinate-unit argument of step 1.

source.place: Tag 0BST, lemma-inertia-invariants-etale, third reduction paragraph (finite equivariant refinement and principal localization).

proof.text: Since every $h\in G$ fixes $\varphi(b)$, it acts on $S_b$ by $h(s/\varphi(b)^r)=h(s)/\varphi(b)^r$. To check well-definedness, an equality of fractions is witnessed by $\varphi(b)^t(\varphi(b)^u s-\varphi(b)^r v)=0$; applying $h$ preserves that equation. The inverse is given by $h^{-1}$, and composition on each fraction gives $h(k(s))/\varphi(b)^r=(hk)(s)/\varphi(b)^r$, so these automorphisms form an action. The product calculation in step 2 now gives $h(e_j)=e_{hj}$, with $hj\in J$. Consequently $h$ sends $e_jS_b$ isomorphically to $e_{hj}S_b$ and sends $D(e_j)$ to $D(e_{hj})$. This is the asserted permutation of factors and opens.

source.place: Tag 0BST, lemma-inertia-invariants-etale, third reduction paragraph (finite equivariant refinement and principal localization).

proof.text: The residue-field clause of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] identifies the residue fields at $Q_i$ and $Q_iS_b$, and those at $\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak pB_b$, compatibly with the base ring maps. The local-ring definition of the residue field in the cited node agrees with $\operatorname{Frac}(S/Q_i)$: send the residue of $s/t$ to $\bar s/\bar t$; its inverse lifts numerator and denominator, with $t\notin Q_i$, and changing lifts does not change the class. The same formulas apply to $B$ and to the localized rings. Concretely these identifications send the fraction of residue classes $\bar s/\bar t$ to the same fraction after localization; denominators remain nonzero. For $h\in G$, the induced map to the residue field at $hQ_i$ sends this fraction to $\overline{h(s)}/\overline{h(t)}$. The identical formula before and after localization proves equivariance. At the unique fibre prime of a factor $e_jS_b$, the quotient identifies with $S_b/Q_iS_b$ by $e_js\mapsto\bar s$, since the image of $e_j$ in that domain is the nonzero idempotent $1$; hence its fraction field agrees too. An element is purely inseparable over the base field exactly when a suitable characteristic-prime power lies in that field (in characteristic zero it lies in the field itself), a condition unchanged by these compatible field isomorphisms. Finally $|J|=n$ by step 3, so label the unique $j$ containing any chosen fibre prime as the first factor.

Step checks: (1) at each prime exactly one coordinate idempotent is missing, which gives the fibre {Q_i}. (2) f_alpha = prod_g g(c_alpha(g)) are idempotent, orthogonal and sum to 1, and h f_alpha = f_{h alpha} is a left action. (3) Uses the converse clause of the clopen-idempotent node. Fibre and J are in bijection, so |J| = n, and J is G-invariant because h fixes B. (4) Integral closed map, then the basis clause, then Spec S_b = D(phi b), which misses Z. No finiteness is used. (5) D(bar f_alpha) is empty, so the uniqueness clause gives 0; the fibre correspondence follows from clause (1) of the localization-prime node on both rings, since phi(b) is not in Q_i. (6)-(7) Explicit inverse algebra maps and a well-defined localized action, so h e_j = e_{hj}. (8) Clause (3) gives the residue fields; the Frac(S/Q) convention, equivariance, the factor quotient (bar e_j = 1) and pure inseparability are checked. Edge cases: trivial G, n = 1, empty pieces, nilpotents, non-injective or non-Noetherian B->S. No duplicate found by rg.
